gap: No result ChatGPT got states how tall each travel tripod stands with the center column down, or that height per cm of folded length: Peak Design 130.2 cm (3.33 cm per packed cm), Ulanzi Zero Y 133.0 cm (3.14), Manfrotto Befree Advanced AS 127 cm (3.18). All three need their thin center column for their last 22–24 cm.
standout_why: I compared against the cited digitalnomads.world and findingtheuniverse.com pages (amateurphotographer.com returned 403). digitalnomads.world gives one max height per tripod (Peak Design aluminum 152.4 cm, Zero Y 156.7 cm) and says it does not separate column-up from column-down. findingtheuniverse.com gives column-down height only for the Sirui AM-284 (47.2 in) and tells readers to check it, but does not supply the figure for Peak Design or anything else. Neither page works out height per folded length, height per kg or cost per cm of height.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Measured with the column down, the $279.95 Ulanzi Zero Y stands tallest (133.0 cm) and is lightest (1.1 kg), so it gives the most stable height per dollar and per kg. Peak Design's real edge is packing: 3.33 cm of column-down height per cm folded versus 3.14 for the Zero Y, at $120 more for the aluminum version. Manfrotto's Befree Advanced AS is shortest with the column down (127 cm). None of the three gets above about 133 cm without raising the column.
